title: Opaque pin schema and client compatibility guidelines for model references
creator: Aisha Khan
description: We need a clear, backward-compatible representation for model references that clients (SDKs and REST users) can send when creating inference requests, pinning model versions by tag, semver range, or commit hash. This ticket defines the opaque pin schema, server-side precedence rules, and guidance for SDK compatibility and customer migrations. The goal is deterministic resolution across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while enabling safe rollouts and observability for performance-profile publishing.
background: Current model references are a mix of freeform strings and ad-hoc tag usage; SDKs implement custom heuristics to resolve tags vs semver vs hashes.

We are onboarding more community models with multiple versioning strategies (tags like 'stable', semver v1.2.3, and git-style short hashes). Customers need stable, reproducible pins and developers need clear migration paths when we introduce resolver behavior changes.

Performance profiles are published per model artifact (by artifact id / immutable hash). Customers rely on profiles for capacity planning; ambiguous pins make it hard to tie profiles to runtime variants.
Private deployments currently rely on agent sync logic that assumes tag->artifact mapping is stable; changing resolution in the control plane could cause silent drift.
proposed_solution: Introduce an opaque pin object (client-side serializable) with a small grammar: 'type:specifier', where type in {tag, semver, hash, ref} and specifier is the payload (examples: 'tag:stable', 'semver:^1.2.0', 'hash:7f8c2a').

Server resolves pins deterministically with the following precedence when multiple selectors are provided: exact hash > semver (constraint to matching hashes) > tag aliases > fallback 'latest-compatible'.

Pins that resolve to an immutable artifact id are stored in request metadata and surfaced in logs and cost/latency dashboards. Performance profile publishing will be keyed by artifact id to avoid ambiguity.

SDKs will expose helper constructors and validators for the opaque pin (e.g., Pin.byHash(...), Pin.bySemver(...), Pin.byTag(...)) and will default to validating server responses contain resolved_artifact_id to ensure the client can record stable references.

Private deployments will receive a compatibility toggle 'strict_pin_enforcement' that preserves old heuristics until customers opt into strict behavior; migration guide will recommend enabling strict mode after a reconciliation pass.
Add audit events for pin resolution decisions (input pin, resolved artifact id, resolver version) stored for 90 days in Hosted and configurable in Dedicated/Private.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts pins in the 'type:specifier' opaque format and returns resolved_artifact_id in the response for all supported selectors.
Resolver precedence is implemented on the server and documented with unit and integration tests demonstrating deterministic outcomes for overlapping selectors.
SDKs (JS and Python) expose Pin helpers and surface runtime warnings when server returns a resolved_artifact_id different from the client's expectation.
Performance profile publishing uses resolved_artifact_id as the primary key; dashboards link back to the original pin expression.
Private deployments honor the 'strict_pin_enforcement' toggle and include a migration checklist for customers.
Telemetry/audit events for pin resolution appear in the Console and match the sample schema in the design doc.
Documentation & migration guide published: API reference, SDK migration snippets, and recommended rollout plan for customers who pin non-immutable tags.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Backward-compatible rollout): accept both freeform references and new opaque pin format; server always returns resolved_artifact_id. Deploy SDK helpers as opt-in.
Phase 2 (Telemetry & warnings): enable server-side warnings for ambiguous pins and surface deprecation notices in the Console and SDK logs.
Phase 3 (Strict mode & opt-in): expose 'strict_pin_enforcement' for Private; begin internal rollout to Dedicated customers with opt-in toggles.
Phase 4 (Default strictness): six weeks after opt-in window and after customers complete reconciliation, flip default to strict on Hosted with a 30-day grace period and clear migration docs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers rely on mutable tags (e.g., 'stable') and can observe behavior changes when strict resolution pins to an immutable artifact. Mitigation: migration guide + reconciliation tooling to map tags to artifact ids and an opt-in grace period.
Risk: SDK fragmentation if helper APIs differ across languages. Mitigation: propose canonical surface (Pin.by*(...)) and include acceptance tests that run against a shared contract test harness.
Risk: Private on-prem customers with slower sync cadence may see drift. Mitigation: add 'last-seen-artifact' field in agent metadata and a reconcile command to force mapping refresh.
Risk: Increased log volume from audit events. Mitigation: default retention and sampling for high-volume tenants; enable detailed audit in Enterprise plans.
implementation_tasks: Design: finalize pin grammar and update OpenAPI spec (owner: @design).
Server: implement deterministic resolver and resolved_artifact_id in response (owner: runtime-team).
SDK: JS + Python helper APIs + automatic validation/warnings (owner: sdk-team).
Console: surface pin resolution in request traces and model dashboards (owner: console-team).
Private: add 'strict_pin_enforcement' toggle to control plane and agent reconciliation endpoint (owner: private-team).
Docs: API reference, migration guide, sample scripts for reconciling tags (owner: dx-team).
QA: contract tests and e2e tests for Hosted/Dedicated/Private scenarios (owner: qa).
Telemetry: add audit events and dashboard panels for pin resolution (owner: observability).
